newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's jobless rate hits three-year high.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's jobless rate hits three-year high.

text.p: South Korea said on Sunday its unemployment rate rose to a three-year high in February in line with a slowing economy, and domestic media reported top business groups would cut new employment by about 30 percent this year.

The jobless rate before taking seasonal factors into account rose to 3.2 percent in the month, sharply higher than 2.3 percent a year earlier, provisional National Statistical Office (NSO) figures showed.
The rate was the highest since February 1994 when it hit the same 3.2 percent. The seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate rose to 2.6 percent compared with 1.9 percent a year ago.
"An economic downturn is largely to blame for the rise," said Lee Hwa-young, deputy director at the office's industrial statistics division.
She said many housewives were now looking for jobs as a business slump eroded job security for their husbands.
"As a result, the economically active female population in February rose by 151,000 from a year ago, while such male population increased by only 137,000," she said.

The National Statistical Office said the total economically active population rose three percent to 20.93 million in February from a year ago, whereas the employed population increased 2.1 percent to 20.27 million.
Local media said the nation's top 30 business conglomerates would cut new employment for this year by about 30 percent in the face of slowing sales growth and falling profit margins.
"Job opportunities will be very slim this year," said a Hyundai Group spokesman.

The National Statistical Office said the faltering economy was also reflected in the nation's industrial output, which rose 6.2 percent year-on-year in February, from an 8.1 percent rise a year earlier.
Factories operated in the month at an average of 79.7 percent of their capacity, against 83.2 percent a year ago.

Output of heavy industrial goods rose a year-on-year 9.7 percent against an 11.2 percent rise a year ago, while that of light industrial goods fell 6.9 percent, against a 3.4 percent fall, the office said.
Private-sector consumption also slowed with wholesale and retail sales rising only 3.3 percent in February, compared with an 11.5 percent rise a year ago, it said.
Investment remained in the doldrums, as seen in falling purchases of machines and equipment.
Domestic machinery orders in February declined 5.6 percent, compared with a 6.0 percent rise a year before, and imports of machinery fell 3.0 percent against a 12.4 percent rise.
Separately, the finance ministry said the consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.5 percent in March on the year, unchanged from a year earlier.
A ministry official said consumer inflation in March reflected stable prices for farm produce. Prices for agricultural, livestock and fisheries products rose a year-on-year 3.8 percent for the month.
Fares for sevices such as private-sector education and public baths rose a year-on-year 5.1 percent, while public utility rates increased 4.4 percent.
Prices for industrial products rose a year-on-year 4.9 percent, led by a 33.2 percent rise in oil products.
Food prices rose a year-on-year 3.6 percent in March, while non-food products increased 5.0 percent, the ministry said.
